title: Google Research UQ Benchmark 2019: Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift, Brier Decomposition & Confidence-Threshold Coverage
author: repo-triad-forge

edges.description: Subproject uq_benchmark_2019 in snapshot google-research-master (archive snapshot, non-git); arXiv:1906.02530
Pairs dataset-shift calibration evaluation, Brier resolution/reliability decomposition, and confidence-threshold accuracy curves with CISC weighted voting
Supports threshold-sweep selective abstention over OOD/shifted inputs
Provides accuracy-vs-threshold selectivity evaluation and Brier resolution/reliability diagnostics
Backfilled canonical module edge (spider follow-up Phase 1 / P0)

claims.assertion: uq_benchmark_2019 benchmarks Vanilla, Temperature Scaling, Deep Ensemble, MC Dropout, SVI, and Last-Layer variants under dataset shift (MNIST-rot, CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, Criteo-corrupt, 20 Newsgroups/LM1B), showing post-hoc temperature scaling falls short under shift relative to model marginalization/ensembles.

metrics_lib.py implements expected_calibration_error(), expected_calibration_error_multiclass(), compute_accuracies_at_confidences() threshold-coverage sweeps, brier_decomposition() into uncertainty/resolution/reliability, and quantile binning with 0->1e-8 guard for np.digitize.

calibration_lib.py fits maximum-likelihood temperature via scipy.optimize.bisect over TF Categorical/Bernoulli NLL gradients in find_scaling_temperature() and applies it via apply_temperature_scaling().

distilled_learning: Evaluate predictive uncertainty under distribution shift using confidence-threshold selectivity sweeps (compute_accuracies_at_confidences) and Brier uncertainty/resolution/reliability decomposition rather than trusting in-distribution temperature scaling alone.
